title: Epidemic early-phase growth tracks R0 and saturates logistically
body:
Early outbreaks of a novel infection grow approximately exponentially at a rate set by the basic reproduction number R0, and saturate as susceptibles deplete.
[Step] Modelling
  [Input] SIR compartments, [Tool] R + deSolve
[Step] Fit
  [Output] R0 ≈ 2.4, final attack rate ≈ 78%
The exponential approximation holds only for the very early phase; once contact reduction or immunity kicks in, the curve bends. SIR is a minimal interpretive scaffold, not a policy-prediction tool — what matters for intervention lives in the structure layered on top of it.
